messages:
alex: Day-0 breadcrumb map — quick reference for access, who-to-ping, and bot notifications. Short version: #help for infra access, DM @sam_it for laptop/ssh, DM @julie_peopleops for badge/hardware, use #eng for product/arch questions, #devex for SDK/docs. Mute noisy bots in channel settings or set DND for heads-down. :wave:

maria: Thanks! My Mac is marked 'ordered' in the portal — is that normal? Do I need to do anything to speed it up?

sam_it: Hey Maria — ordering is normal. If you need expedited ship, DM me and I can flip priority. Also check the onboarding portal: click "Device requests" > "Order status".

maria: Got it. Also, VPN/how-to connect?

sam_it: VPN steps quick:

```
1) Install WireGuard from https://wireguard.com/install
2) Pull profile from https://onboard.redwood.io/vpn (SSO)
3) Import profile into WireGuard and connect

If you hit authentication errors, run: `curl -v https://onboard.redwood.io/me` to confirm SSO cookie.
```

it-bot: Provision request #12345 created for maria — laptop order tracked. ETA 2 business days. :package:

alex: Note on channel etiquette: when you have an access or onboarding question, post in-thread in #new-hires or use #help for infra stuff. Avoid cross-posting the same question in multiple channels — it fragments answers. If the question is team-specific, ping the team channel (e.g., #eng or #eng-infra) and include a one-line summary and the ID of any open ticket.

julie_peopleops: For badge/office access: send me your full name + badge photo in a DM and I'll create the request. For equipment swaps or peripherals, open a ticket at https://support.redwoodinfra/requests and tag "hardware".

maria: Where do I mute the onboarding bots? I'm getting a lot of notifications from #deploy-bot.

alex: Two quick ways: 1) Go to the channel header > Notifications > Mute channel (this mutes channel pings). 2) Use Slack DND when deep focus: `/dnd 60m` or `/dnd until 9am` for overnight. For specific bot messages, you can click the message > More actions > Mute @bot-name if offered.

maria: Nice. Any rules about @channel/@here?

alex: Use @channel rarely — only for page-impacting notices or agreed team-wide events. Use @here for immediate on-site needs during core hours. When in doubt, DM a small set of folks or post in #help and @ the oncall alias if it's urgent.

sam_it: One more practical trick — if a bot is spamming you from a subscription, open the channel details > Integrations and disable the specific bot for your view, or unsubscribe via the bot's config message (often a "unsubscribe" link or a reaction command).

ops-bot: Reminder: new-hires checklist — complete SSO, join 2FA group, confirm laptop serial in portal.

alex: Final tips: pin the onboarding docs to #new-hires for quick links, add yourself to the "Onboarded" user group once done, and please drop a one-line intro in #introductions with your pronouns and a fun fact. Welcome aboard! :tada:
